items.title: DRFLOW: A Deep Research Benchmark for Personalized Workflow Prediction
items.summary_1line: Deep research (DR) systems are increasingly used for complex information-seeking tasks, but existing works mainly focus on generating reports and summaries. In contrast, many enterprise tasks instead require an agent...
items.editor_note: Redefines the goal toward enterprise needs: DRFLOW benchmarks personalized workflow prediction rather than report or summary generation.

editorial.tldr: In mid-June, deep research agents got pushed on both evaluation and engineering. An arXiv paper argued that existing benchmarks only grade a single-shot report and miss whether an agent improves when given feedback, and ran a multi-turn evaluation under process-level feedback. AWS then shipped a concrete build pattern: an end-to-end competitive research agent on Deep Agents and Bedrock AgentCore with isolated execution for multi-step workflows. The latest beat, DRFLOW, reframes the target again, arguing real enterprise work needs the agent to predict a personalized workflow rather than just produce a report, and proposing a benchmark for it.
editorial.whats_new: The newest item, DRFLOW (Jun 16), moves the benchmark goalposts past report generation toward predicting personalized, enterprise-style workflows — a different success criterion than the feedback-driven report quality the Jun 8 paper measured.
editorial.why_it_matters: How you evaluate a deep research agent is still unsettled: single-shot report quality, improvement under process-level feedback, and personalized workflow prediction are three different bars, and the one you pick changes what you build. AWS's Deep Agents + Bedrock AgentCore walkthrough is a ready reference for the isolated-execution, multi-step plumbing underneath any of them.
